text: {"decision":"GO","artifact":{"author":"Graham Hill","capacity":"Individual author","audience":"Business and IT leaders","as_of":"2026-10-09","title":"Valid credentials can carry invalid intent","reported_facts":["A payment request can arrive from whitelisted infrastructure, use valid credentials and still be fraudulent. CERT-In reported campaigns in which attackers stole payment credentials and invoked fund-transfer APIs from compromised organizations’ own infrastructure, bypassing application-level checks. It also reported dummy transaction references with no corresponding records. [CIAD-2026-0046, 2026-10-09]","Cloudflare’s earlier incident account shows a different failure of inherited trust: credentials stolen in the October 2023 Okta compromise were mistakenly considered unused and left unrotated. Attackers subsequently used them to access its Atlassian environment. Cloudflare reported that segmentation and other controls limited lateral movement, with no customer data or global network changes affected. [CF2024, 2024-02-01]"],"inference":"Previously trusted access stops being reliable evidence of legitimate action when someone can reuse that access outside the conditions that justified trusting it. A recognized credential and an approved network location can establish how a request arrived; they cannot, by themselves, establish that the business action was authorized. These two accounts support that distinction without establishing a common attacker or identical failure.","recommendation_as_of_cutoff":"For leaders approving payment systems, ask what independently proves that each payout belongs to an approved transaction. Require payout validation against sanctioned records, cryptographic binding between validation and debit stages, second-level verification, and transaction and daily limits at the payment API itself. CERT-In recommended these measures on October 9, 2026; its advisory does not demonstrate their measured effectiveness. Credential rotation and removal of long-lived static tokens address the access side of the problem. Near-real-time reconciliation and automated holds on suspicious transfers address detection and response.
